We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have guidance: reactions enumerated in order to be applied forward: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution (halogenation). But we need to do retrosynthesis (reverse). So we need to break target into precursors via three steps, likely corresponding to those forward reactions reversed.

Thus step1 (retro) would be Sn2 reverse: break C-N bond formed by SN2 (i.e., disconnection of C-N to give a halide (Cl) on carbon and amine as nucleophile). So we need to replace a C-N bond with C-Cl (or C-Br) and amine.

Look at target: there is an anilide: NC(=O) attached to aromatic ring (anisole). The amide nitrogen attached to carbonyl which attached to heterocycle (c2nnn...). The amide N is attached to aromatic ring (aniline). The C-N bond we could break is the N-aryl bond? But SN2 typically on aliphatic carbon. Maybe the side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to heterocycle via CH2 (C attached to heterocycle). That CH2 is attached to heterocycle nitrogen? Actually heterocycle: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine? It's a 1,2,4-triazine? The substituent is Cc3... attached to N of triazine? The pattern: nnn(Cc3...) indicates N attached to CH2-aryl. So there is a C-N bond between N of triazine and CH2 of phenyl. That could be formed via SN2 (alkyl halide + amine). So retro step: break that C-N to give halide on benzylic carbon (Cl-CH2-aryl) and amine (triazine N-H). So precursor1: halide benzylic chloride (ClCH2-aryl) and triazine with NH (instead of N-alkyl). Good.

Second step: Friedel-Crafts acylation: maybe formation of amide bond? Actually forward Friedel-Crafts acylation introduces acyl onto aromatic ring, breaking halide (acyl chloride). In our target, we have anisole ring with amide substituent (NC(=O)...). That could be formed by acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from heterocycle? But Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl to aromatic ring, not amide. However we have anilide (aryl-NH-CO-...). Could be formed by substitution of halogen on aromatic ring with amide via nucleophilic aromatic substitution? Not typical. Maybe the forward sequence: first substitution to convert phenol to halide, then SN2 to attach amine, then Friedel-Crafts to attach acyl? The guidance says order enumerated forward: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution. So forward: first SN2 (makes C-N), then Friedel-Crafts acylation (makes C-C acyl), then substitution (replace OH with halogen). So retrosynthesis reverse order: start from target, first undo substitution (i.e., replace halide with OH), then undo Friedel-Crafts acylation (remove acyl group), then undo SN2 (break C-N). So three steps.

Thus step1 retro: substitution reversal: identify a halide functional group that was introduced. In target, we have no halide. But maybe there is a chlorine on aromatic ring? Not present. However there is a fluorine on piperidine ring (N4CC(F)C4). That fluorine could be from substitution of OH? Not typical. Could be from halogenation of alkyl? The substitution step could be converting an alcohol to halide (e.g., OH to Cl). In target we have a fluorine, not chlorine. Could be that step is halogenation of an alcohol to give fluorine? Not typical. Maybe the substitution step is converting a hydroxyl to a fluorine via DAST etc. But guidance says halide functional group (Cl, Br, I). So maybe the target originally had a chlorine that got replaced later? Not present.

Alternative: maybe the substitution step is converting a phenol (OH) to a methoxy (OCH3) via halogen? Not.

Given complexity, perhaps we can propose a plausible retrosynthesis using known transformations: 1) Disconnection of benzylic C-N (SN2) to give benzylic chloride and triazine NH. 2) Disconnection of amide bond via reverse Friedel-Crafts acylation: break C=O attached to aromatic ring to give aniline (aniline with NH2) and acyl chloride derived from heterocycle (i.e., carbonyl attached to triazine). So precursor: aniline (anisole ring with NH2) and acyl chloride (C(=O)Cl attached to triazine). 3) Substitution: convert anisole methoxy? Actually we have methoxy on aromatic ring (CO-). That could be from O-methylation of phenol (substitution). So reverse substitution: phenol (OH) to methoxy. So final precursor: phenol (hydroxy anisole) and maybe halide? Not.

Thus propose route:

Target -> step1 (retro SN2): break N-CH2 bond to give benzylic chloride (ClCH2-Ph-... with CN4CC(F)C4 attached) and triazine with NH (c2nnn(C)??). Actually the triazine after removal of CH2 becomes c2nnn(c2N)?? The substituent becomes just H? The triazine originally has N-alkyl and also an exocyclic NH2 (c2nnn(... )c2N). So after removal, we have triazine with NH (still). So precursor A: Cl-CH2-Ph-CN4CC(F)C4 (benzylic chloride) and triazine core with NH (c2nnn(c2N)??). We'll need to check.

Step2 (retro Friedel-Crafts acylation): break amide bond between aromatic ring and carbonyl attached to triazine. So we get aniline (anisole ring with NH2) and acyl chloride derived from triazine (Cl-CO-c2nnn(... )c2N). That acyl chloride can be used in Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach to anisole.

Step3 (retro substitution): convert methoxy to hydroxy (demethylation) to give phenol (hydroxy anisole). So final precursors: phenol (HO- anisole) and aniline? Wait we already have aniline after step2. Actually step2 gave aniline (with NH2) and acyl chloride. The aniline still has methoxy? The methoxy is on the aromatic ring (CO-). So after step3, we would have phenol (HO- anisole) with NH2? Actually the aromatic ring has both methoxy and amide substituent. After step2, we have anisole ring with NH2 (instead of amide) and methoxy unchanged. So step3 demethylates methoxy to OH, giving phenol with NH2. So final precursors: phenol (HO- anisole) and acyl chloride (triazine). But we also need the benzylic chloride and triazine? Wait step2 uses acyl chloride derived from triazine (which still has the N-alkyl substituent? Actually after step1, the triazine lost the benzylic substituent, so acyl chloride would be attached to triazine with NH2 and maybe no substituent. So step2 uses that triazine acyl chloride.

Thus overall three precursors: (1) phenol (4-methoxy? Actually 4-methoxy? The anisole is at position 1? The SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)... )c1. So methoxy at position 1, amide at position 5. So phenol would be HOc1cccc(NH2?) Wait after step2, the amide is removed, leaving NH2 at that position? Actually the amide is attached to aromatic carbon; after removal, that carbon becomes attached to NH2? No, the amide carbonyl is attached to aromatic carbon via C-N bond (aryl-NH-CO-). If we break amide, we get aniline (aryl-NH2) and acyl chloride. So the aromatic carbon now has NH2 substituent. So final phenol would have both OH (from methoxy) and NH2 (from amide). So final precursor: 2,5-dihydroxy? Actually positions: methoxy at ortho? Not needed.

Thus final precursors: 4-methoxy-2-aminophenol? Let's generate SMILES: COc1ccc(N)cc1? Wait methoxy at position 1, amine at position 5 (para). So SMILES: COc1ccc(N)cc1. That's anisidine (4-methoxyaniline). But we need phenol after demethylation: HOc1ccc(N)cc1 (4-aminophenol). So final precursor: 4-aminophenol.

Other precursor: acyl chloride derived from triazine core (with NH2). SMILES: ClC(=O)c2nnn(c2N). Actually carbonyl attached to triazine carbon? The triazine is aromatic heterocycle; the acyl chloride attaches to carbonyl carbon attached to triazine? The target has NC(=O)c2nnn(... )c2N. So the carbonyl carbon attached to triazine carbon (c2). So acyl chloride would be ClC(=O)c2nnn(... )c2N. After step1, the N-alkyl substituent removed, so the triazine has N-H and maybe no substituent. So acyl chloride: ClC(=O)c2nnn(c2N). We'll need to include the N-alkyl substituent later via SN2.

Thus step1 precursor: benzylic chloride: ClCH2-Ph-CN4CC(F)C4 attached to phenyl ring (the phenyl attached to CH2). The phenyl is part of the substituent attached to triazine via CH2. So the benzylic chloride SMILES: ClCC1=CC=C(CN4CC(F)C4)C=C1. That's 4-(fluoromorpholine?) Actually N4CC(F)C4 is azetidine? It's a four-membered ring? N4CC(F)C4 is azetidine with fluorine. So we have benzylic chloride attached to phenyl bearing that side chain.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type mol root target, children reaction nodes with template IDs. We need template IDs for each reaction. We have found template ID 1914393 corresponds to SN2 (Cl-CH2-aryl + amine -> N-alkyl). That matches our SN2 step. So step1 retro uses that template (reverse direction). So we will use template_id 1914393.

Step2 Friedel-Crafts acylation template? Need to find a template for Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride. Search for functional_groups_broken halide and bonds_formed C-C? Let's search for "acyl chloride" maybe template with acylation.
